title: Calling Business Central APIs Without a Client Secret
summary: Explains how an Azure Function or Static Web App backend can call Business Central APIs without a client secret: the function gets a managed identity token, then exchanges it via a federated credential on the app registration for a token that BC accepts. The author notes this still works but a newer post describes a better way that calls BC directly from a managed identity.
key_points: Managed identities assigned to Azure resources can obtain access tokens without needing client secrets
Federated credentials enable token exchange between the managed identity token and an app registration token
An Entra Application must still be created in Business Central with appropriate permission sets
Token exchange uses JWT bearer assertion to swap a managed identity token for an app registration token
Establishes trust between managed identity issuer and app registration to authorize the token exchange

quotes.text: We need to exchange the token we've already got for a token issued for the app registration.
quotes.why_it_matters: This explains the core mechanism: the managed identity token alone is insufficient; it must be exchanged for an app registration token that has Business Central permissions.

quotes.text: It would be better if we had a solution that didn't rely on client secrets.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the motivation: avoiding secrets eliminates expiration management, key vault dependencies, and credential compromise risks.
